title: spec/appendix-ccp12-hopping.md: Python example uses max(...,1) but pseudocode uses MAX(...,2) causing interoperability bug
description:
The pseudocode at lines 84 and 159 specifies N = MAX(NChannels - 1, 2), but the Python example at line 305 uses n = max(n_channels - 1, 1). When NChannels = 2, pseudocode yields N=2 (selecting channels 1 or 2) while Python yields n=1 (always selecting channel 1). Implementations following different parts of this spec will fail to rendezvous.

Fix suggestion: Change line 305 to: n = max(n_channels - 1, 2) to match the pseudocode
close_reason: Already fixed: Python example at line 304 uses max(n_channels - 1, 2), which matches the pseudocode at lines 85 and 159. All three locations consistently use minimum value 2.
